title: Crosswalker Import Recipe
description: The shape of an import recipe. A recipe is the deterministic, declarative spec that tells a Crosswalker producer how to project a source ontology onto a Tier 1 vault. Closed grammar of five mechanisms (folder/file/heading/tag/wikilink) × ordered layout × cross-cutting also_emit × optional graph_edges. Per Ch 22 target-structure synthesis (2026-05-04). Engine implementations (the plugin's bundled TypeScript engine, an external Python CLI, an AI agent) all consume this same schema; recipe semantics are runtime-agnostic.
$comment: v0.1. JSON Schema 2020-12. Stable URI; breaking changes will bump to /v2/. SchemaVer 1.17.0. Additive history: 1.1.0 (2026-05-09, v0.1.6) added the optional `query:` block per Ch 31; 1.2.0 (2026-07-05) added the optional `variadic` folder-expansion block on layout_entry per the variadic-split design; 1.3.0 (2026-07-10, v0.1.6) added the optional `target.also_emit.frontmatter.managed_links` (list-valued managed wikilink arrays, for multi-value link columns) and the optional `target.enrichment` block (batch-scope Pass 1.5 enrichment: children lists, facet hub notes, parent-note placement) per the 2026-07-10 batch-enrichment design; 1.4.0 (2026-07-11) added the optional `target.enrichment.level_hubs` (hierarchy hub/MOC index notes, one per folder level) and `target.enrichment.waypoint_marker` (opt-in `%% Waypoint %%` marker on generated folder-note/hub notes) per the 2026-07-11 ICSB emitter-controls gap audit; 1.5.0 (2026-07-21) added optional display metadata with structured `based_on` ancestry, optional source compatibility version, and ordered `target.also_emit.body` projections. 1.6.0 (2026-08-21) added the optional and curie-prefix(prefix) template filters for omission-safe stable identity fields. 1.7.0 (2026-08-26) extended $defs/template only (no structural change): ['segment'] literal-key quoting at any path position, `optional` widened to fire at every path segment, list-valued interpolations with automatic per-item filter lifting, the split(delimiter)/join(separator)/reject(pattern)/wikilink/trim(chars) filter forms, and balanced-paren + backslash lexing of filter arguments, per the 2026-08-26 template-engine contract. 1.8.0 (2026-08-26) added the optional `target.auto_heading` (a template string sets the automatic H1 text, `false` suppresses it, omitted preserves prior behaviour byte-for-byte including the recipe-path/wizard-path conditional difference) per the same 2026-08-26 template-engine contract. 1.9.0 (2026-08-27) added the optional `source.where` (a JSONata row predicate over the raw source row, evaluated before identity/CURIE/concept_cid/render, loud on a non-boolean result, on an unknown field reference, and on admitting zero rows; participates in the recipe hash because it changes which notes exist) per the 2026-08-27 Ch 46 source contract. `source.joins` (optional named secondary collections located inside the same source bytes, indexed by a key expression, binding under an alias that never merges into or shadows the primary row namespace; loud on an undefined, empty or non-scalar key, legitimately empty on no match; participates in the recipe hash for the same reason) landed in the same 1.9.0 step. 1.10.0 (2026-09-06) added the optional `metadata.based_on.recipe_document_digest`, a strict digest of the complete normalized canonical ancestor recipe document. 1.11.0 (2026-09-15) extended $defs/template only: the part(delimiters,index), part(delimiters) and prefix(delimiters,index) filters, which split on any single character of a delimiter set; prefix keeps the original delimiters. Additive; existing recipes validate unchanged. 1.12.0 (2026-09-21): additive. target.crosswalks[] (cross-ontology references in a concept column, emitted as crosswalk_edge notes in their own import set; distinct from graph_edges, which are concept-note frontmatter) and source.detect (offer-only source recognition hints: sheet, sheet_aliases, header_row, filename, notes). Existing recipes validate unchanged; a recipe without either key hashes byte-identically. 1.13.0 (2026-09-21): additive. source.nest[] (nested record levels: one row per record at every level, each carrying a reserved _cw lineage object; per-level id template, children field or join source, carry, leaf, identity) and $defs/source_join_from hoisted from source_join.from with unchanged semantics. Existing recipes validate unchanged; a recipe without nest hashes byte-identically. 1.14.0 (2026-09-22): additive. nest_level.leaf gains 'section' (a level folded into its nearest note-bearing ancestor's body as heading regions, via that level's layout heading entry) and body_entry (append) gains optional level. Existing recipes validate unchanged; a recipe without either hashes byte-identically. 1.15.0 (2026-09-23): additive edge endpoint projection convention: bundled crosswalk-edge recipes declare optional managed subject_note and object_note scalar wikilinks and a managed body line resolved from concept CURIE identity at write time. No new grammar or required keys; recipes without these projections validate and hash byte-identically. 1.16.0 (2026-09-23): additive $contains(value, 'literal') in source predicates; the second argument must be a string literal, never a regex or a dynamic pattern. Recipes that omit this function validate and hash byte-identically. 1.17.0 (2026-09-23): additive. layout_entry.implied_concept (implied concept level: a folder level whose concepts have no source row; each distinct rendered value becomes a concept note at <folder>/<label>.md with curie <prefix>:<identity>). Legal on folder entries only, never the leaf, not with variadic. Optional enrichment.parent_links defaults on for implied levels and may be set false. Participates in the recipe hash through target.layout. Existing recipes validate and hash byte-identically.

recipe_document_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of a complete validated canonical recipe after Crosswalker normalization. The hashed bytes are the full recursively key-sorted JSON object, including normalized defaults, source, target, metadata, ancestry references and array order. This is distinct from the reduced effective-target recipe hash.

mechanism.description: How a source level lands in the target vault. 'folder': directory segment. 'file': leaf-bearing markdown file. 'heading': intra-file '#'-prefixed anchor. 'tag': nested tag-path segment. 'wikilink': flat file with explicit parent/child wikilink edges in frontmatter. v0.1 wires folder/file/heading; tag and wikilink as layout mechanisms are schema-reserved and ship in v0.2 (validators reject them as 'mechanism not yet implemented; coming in v0.2' in v0.1 to avoid silent corruption).

template.description: R2RML-style template with {var} interpolation. Variables come from the source level scope (e.g., {control.id}, {family.title}, {col}). PATHS: a path is a sequence of segments separated by '.'. A segment is bare (dotted traversal into nested source data, e.g. {external_references.0.external_id}) or QUOTED for a literal key, written ['segment'] (SchemaVer 1.7.0). Quoting is per segment, so it composes with traversal at any depth: {['CRI Profile v2.2 Diagnostic Statement']}, {objects.0.['external-id']}, {['weird.parent'].child.['odd.leaf']}. Inside a quoted segment \' is a literal quote and \\ a backslash. As a compatibility affordance, an all-bare dotted path whose whole raw text is an own key of the row (a dotted CSV/XLSX header) resolves to that column; the quoted form is the normative way to say so, and a competing nested reading is reported rather than silently preferred. FILTERS: lower, upper, title, slug, tagsafe, fs-safe, truncate(N), trim, trim(chars), number, split(delimiter,index), split(delimiter), part(delimiters,index), part(delimiters), prefix(delimiters,index), regex(pattern), reject(pattern), join(separator), wikilink, curie-prefix(prefix), plus first-position optional as a missing-value control. part(delimiters,index) returns the 0-based piece of the trimmed value after splitting on ANY single character of the delimiter set, dropping empty pieces; an index past the last piece yields an empty value with a render note. part(delimiters) produces the list of non-empty trimmed pieces, like split(delimiter). prefix(delimiters,index) returns the original value truncated right after the end of the indexed piece, keeping the original delimiters in the prefix (GV.OC-01.01 with delimiters '.-' and index 2 gives GV.OC-01). {var|optional} resolves a missing/null path to an empty value AT ANY SEGMENT (SchemaVer 1.7.0); ordinary missing variables still fail. {var|optional|curie-prefix(nist)} omits an absent identity and prefixes a present local value. LISTS (SchemaVer 1.7.0): a value may be a list, and every filter maps over it automatically, so {related|optional|split(,)|trim(.)|reject(^\[None\]$)|curie-prefix(nist-800-53)} cleans, drops and prefixes each item. split(delimiter) produces a list; join(separator) consumes one; reject(pattern) drops items; wikilink wraps each item in [[...]]. Items that a filter blanks are elided. A list may land in also_emit.frontmatter.managed (YAML array), managed_links (link array) or a body projection with format 'list'; reaching any text template it is an error naming join. Filter arguments are lexed with balanced parentheses and backslash escapes, so regex(:\s*(.+)$) and regex(A|B) are written as one would write the regex; \) \( \| \, \\ emit the single character and any other backslash pair is passed through intact. Computation beyond filters escapes into the Function primitive (Ch 20).

level_depth.description: Markdown heading depth (1-6, equivalent to # through ######). Required when mechanism is 'heading'. Ignored otherwise.

recipe_metadata.title: Recipe display metadata
recipe_metadata.description: Optional artifact display metadata and structured ancestry. Application/session origin is intentionally not serialized here. This block is excluded from the effective target hash.

based_on.title: Recipe ancestry reference
based_on.description: Structured reference to the recipe this artifact was customized from. Unrelated to inferred or derived crosswalk mappings.

recipe.description: Stable identifier of the ancestor recipe.

hash.description: Optional effective-target hash receipt for the ancestor recipe.

recipe_document_digest.description: Optional digest of the complete normalized canonical ancestor recipe named by `recipe`.

spec_version.description: Optional recipe-spec URI receipt for the ancestor recipe.

body_entry.title: Body projection entry
body_entry.description: One ordered, recipe-managed body projection. Body is cross-cutting output, not a sixth layout mechanism. `table-row` and legacy transforms are intentionally excluded until a portable table/transform grammar exists.

position.description: Append formatted content without a section heading. Omitted position defaults to append.

omit_if_empty.description: When true (default), omit the region if the rendered template is empty.

level.description: Restricts this projection to the records of one nest level that declares leaf: section; rendered once per attached record, against that record's scope, under its heading. Absent: applies to every emitted row as before.

heading.description: Literal section heading text. Templated headings are not admitted in this schema version.

omit_if_empty.description: When false, an empty section still emits its heading.

variadic.title: Variadic folder expansion
variadic.description: Variable-depth folder expansion for a folder layout entry. A fixed layout lists its folder levels ahead of time (one entry per level); ragged ids (e.g. ATT&CK 'T1055' vs 'T1055.011') carry a different number of pieces per row, so no fixed list fits every row. `variadic` explodes the entry's rendered scalar AFTER templating (templates stay scalar) into a variable number of folder levels. Valid ONLY on mechanism 'folder' (enforced by the layout_entry allOf if/then). Additive in SchemaVer 1.2.0; recipes without `variadic` continue to validate. Deterministic: segments derive only from the row's own value. Per the 2026-07-05 variadic-split design.

delimiter.description: Delimiter the rendered scalar is split on. Example: '.' for ATT&CK technique ids ('T1055.011').

segment.description: Folder-name shape per segment. 'prefix' (default): cumulative prefixes joined by the delimiter ('X.Y.Z' → 'X', 'X.Y') — globally-unique names, matches the CSF recipe convention. 'part': raw pieces ('X.Y.Z' → 'X', 'Y').

drop_last.description: Drop the final piece before building folders (default true) — the leaf belongs to the file entry, which names it with the full id anyway.

max_depth.description: Safety cap on the number of folder levels produced.

on_overflow.description: What to do when the split produces more than max_depth segments. 'truncate' (default): keep the first max_depth, record a deviation note (no data loss — the full id is in the filename). 'error': fail the render.

layout_entry.title: Layout entry
layout_entry.description: One entry of the recipe.target.layout array. Specifies how a single source level lands in the target vault. The layout array is ordered: outer source levels appear first, leaf-bearing entry appears last (typically mechanism: 'file' or 'heading' for the leaf-as-document case). Per Ch 22, the leaf entry MAY declare a `kind` to produce non-concept Tier 1 shapes (junction notes for evidence links, crosswalk edges for ontology mappings); intermediate entries treat `kind` as ignored. Default `kind` is 'concept'.

level.description: Source-level identifier. Must match an entry in recipe.source.levels. Examples: 'catalog', 'family', 'control', 'enhancement', 'taxon'.

kind.description: Tier 1 shape produced by this layout entry. 'concept' (default): standard concept-note (control/term/taxon/etc.); produces concept_note_frontmatter per spec/tier1.schema.json. 'junction-note': evidence-link triple (subject_concept, predicate, evidence_doc); 13-field schema. 'crosswalk-edge': between-ontology mapping; STRM predicate vocabulary + SSSOM-shaped envelope. Recipe authors typically declare `kind` on the leaf layout entry only — intermediate folder/heading entries leave it default.

implied_concept.description: An implied concept level: a folder whose concept has no source row. One concept note is emitted per distinct rendered folder value unless a row produces its curie. true uses the rendered folder value as identity; the object form renders an identity template against each describing row, requiring agreement. Identity is never inferred from a vault path. Additive SchemaVer 1.17.0.

identity.description: Template for the curie local part; defaults to the rendered folder value.

graph_edge.title: Graph edge
graph_edge.description: One frontmatter-encoded relationship between two concepts. Used to express hierarchy or named relations as data (parent, enhances, partOf, instanceOf, crosswalksTo) rather than as folder structure. Semantically aligned with SKOS broader/narrower and ISO 25964 BTG/BTP/BTI. Schema-reserved in v0.1; wired in v0.2.

via.description: Frontmatter property name encoding the relation. Conventional values: 'parent', 'enhances', 'partOf', 'instanceOf', 'crosswalksTo (intra-vault convenience only; cross-ontology references belong in target.crosswalks)', 'broader', 'narrower'. Recipe authors pick a value that matches their query intent.

crosswalk_entry.title: Crosswalk column entry
crosswalk_entry.description: One cross-ontology reference column of a concept source and how to read it. See target.crosswalks.

to_ontology.description: CURIE prefix of the target ontology, e.g. nist-csf-2.

qualifier.description: What to do with a parenthetical after an id.

frontmatter_block.title: Frontmatter projection rules
frontmatter_block.description: What frontmatter the recipe writes onto each output note, plus which keys it preserves on re-render. The managed/user_preserve split is load-bearing: managed keys are recipe-owned (overwritten on every re-render because they are projections of canonical source state); user_preserve keys are user-owned (never overwritten because they are user annotations introduced after the import).

managed.description: Recipe-owned frontmatter. Keys → templates. Re-render overwrites these. Example: { framework: 'nist-800-53-r5', control_id: '{control.id}', family: '{family.id}' }.

managed_links.description: Recipe-owned, list-valued managed wikilink arrays (additive SchemaVer 1.3.0). Each key maps to a template plus optional split delimiters; the rendered value is split on those delimiters, each non-empty piece is wrapped in [[...]], and the key is emitted as a YAML array of wikilink strings. Used for multi-value link columns (e.g. a 'Related Controls' cell 'AC-2, AC-3, PM-9' → related: ['[[AC-2]]', '[[AC-3]]', '[[PM-9]]']). Single-value links stay in `managed` as scalar '[[...]]' strings. Re-render regenerates the array wholesale (managed, not unioned). Recipes without this key validate unchanged.

split.description: Delimiters the rendered value is split on before wikilinking each piece. Default when omitted: comma and semicolon.

user_preserve.description: User-owned frontmatter key patterns. Re-render preserves these untouched. Glob patterns ('*notes*') or exact keys ('reviewer', 'status', 'evidence_links'). Default if omitted: empty (no preservation).

items.description: Frontmatter key (or glob) to preserve. Example: 'reviewer', 'status', '*-notes', '*'.

enrichment.title: Batch enrichment (Pass 1.5)
enrichment.description: Optional batch-scope enrichment applied after every row renders (additive SchemaVer 1.3.0). render() stays pure and per-row; enrichment derives cross-row artifacts (children lists on parents, materialized facet hub notes) that no single row can know. Deterministic: same rows in → same vault out, with every derived list sorted by curie so input order never leaks. Recipes without this block emit no enrichment and validate unchanged. Per the 2026-07-10 batch-enrichment design.

parent_links.description: When an implied concept level is declared, add managed parent and parent_curie links to nested notes using the parent concept identity rather than a path. Omitted means on for such recipes; false disables these links without changing which concept notes exist. Recipes without implied concept levels retain their old output.

children_lists.description: When true, every parent note gains a managed `children` array of wikilinks to its direct children (derived from the same parent relation the parent link uses), sorted by child curie. Regenerated wholesale on re-import (fully managed, not unioned).

facet_notes.description: How facet values materialize. 'none': nothing beyond the per-note facet tags. 'tags-only': facet tags only, no hub notes. 'notes': one synthetic hub note per facet value with a managed `members` list of its member notes (sorted by curie), a `kind: facet` discriminator, the facet tag, and an H1 body; user prose below the H1 survives re-import. Hub notes are emitted only for facet values with two or more members.

parent_note.description: Where a concept that is also a parent of other concepts lives. 'sibling': the concept note sits beside its children's folder (X.md next to X/). 'folder-note': the concept note moves inside its own folder as X/X.md via the batch enrichment pass. Relocation is evidence-based (applies only to parents whose children actually nest under their own-named folder), re-import write targets resolve by curie so relocated parents never duplicate, and flipping back to 'sibling' relocates symmetrically. Streamed sources fall back to 'sibling' with a deviation note (relocation requires the eager batch).

hub_note_folder.description: Optional vault-relative folder for materialized facet hub notes. When omitted, hub notes land at the output root beside the imported concepts.

level_hubs.description: Hierarchy hub/MOC index notes (additive SchemaVer 1.4.0, 2026-07-11 ICSB emitter-controls gap audit). 'none': no hierarchy index notes. 'notes': every folder level in the generated structure gets an index note derived from the model, never a filesystem scan. A folder whose own concept note already exists in the batch (sibling or folder-note shaped) HOSTS its index: that note gains a managed body 'Contents' section listing the folder's direct children. A folder with no such note (a pure structural grouping folder, or the per-import root) gets a brand-new hub note (`kind: 'hub'`) at `<folder>/<folder>.md`. Deterministic and re-import safe: the managed section is stripped and reappended by delimiter markers, same discipline as `facet_notes`.

waypoint_marker.description: Also append the `%% Waypoint %%` trigger comment to every folder-note/hub note this import generates (additive SchemaVer 1.4.0). Opt-in and additive to `level_hubs` — Crosswalker's own managed section stays the primary, always-on connectivity mechanism; this only lets the Waypoint community plugin additionally track notes a user later adds to that folder by hand. Idempotent across re-imports; never strips a `%% Begin Waypoint %%` block Waypoint itself has already expanded.

source_join_from.title: Secondary collection
source_join_from.description: Where the secondary collection lives, INSIDE THE SAME SOURCE BYTES: another sheet of the same workbook, or a sibling array of the same JSON document. Exactly one of sheet or iterator. A single-collection source such as CSV has no second collection to name and is rejected.

sheet.description: Name of another sheet in the same workbook.

header_row.description: 0-based index of the header row on that sheet, skipping banner rows above it. Sheets in one workbook differ in banner depth. Applies to sheet only; declaring it beside iterator is an error rather than a silently ignored key.

iterator.description: Iterator path locating a sibling array of the same JSON document, e.g. $.response.elements.relationships[*]. Same closed grammar as the primary iterator: dotted keys plus [*] fan-out.

where.description: Optional JSONata predicate over the SECONDARY rows, with exactly the contract of source.where: same restricted subset, must return a boolean, every referenced field must exist in the secondary collection, and admitting zero rows is an error. This is how one shared relationship table is narrowed to a single predicate before it is indexed. Fixed depth: there is no nested joins here.

nest_level.title: Nested record level
nest_level.description: One level of a nested source. See source.nest.

level.description: Name of this level; must appear in source.levels and be used by target.layout.

id.description: Template for this level's stable identifier, evaluated against the record. Example: {id} for OSCAL, {control_id} for CIS.

oneOf.description: JSON: the field on this level's record that holds the next level's array. Example: controls, then parts.
Workbook or sibling-array: where the next level's records live; joined to this level by the next entry's parent_key.

parent_key.description: When children came from a join: the child field that holds the parent's id. Required for join-sourced levels; ignored for JSON field children.

carry.description: Fields of this level's record that child rows may read under _cw.ancestors.<level>.<field>. Default: the id field only. Keep it short; this is how a part note can name its control's title.

leaf.description: How this level's own record is emitted. 'folder-note': the row renders the layout entries at or above its level and lands as <folder>/<folder>.md. 'none': this level produces no row or note of its own (its children still carry _cw.parent naming it). 'section': this level's records are not emitted as rows; each is attached to its nearest emitted ancestor's row under _cw.sections (document order) and rendered as a heading region inside that ancestor's managed body, using this level's layout heading entry for heading text and depth and the body projections declared with level: <this level> for content. Legal on any level whose parent is a note or a section level; never on level 0. Required on every non-leaf level unless target.layout declares a file entry for that level; a non-leaf level with neither is refused at validation.

identity.description: How this level's CURIE local part is formed. 'global': the id template's value as is; use when the id is unique across the whole source (OSCAL control ids). 'path': _cw.path pieces joined with '/', each piece escaped first so the join is injective; use when ids repeat under different parents (a part called 'statement' under every control). Fixed at import-set mint like every identity rule; a refresh cannot flip it.

source_join.title: Keyed lookup enrichment
source_join.description: One named secondary collection, indexed by a key expression, whose matched rows bind under the alias on every primary row that matches. Keyed lookup enrichment only, never relational algebra: one primary stream plus N independent bounded indexes, fixed depth, no nested joins. A two-hop join (A to B to C) is deliberately not expressible: hop 2's key would depend on hop 1's result set, which is join composing with join. Denormalize in the producer instead.

on.title: Key match
on.description: The key both sides are matched on. Both expressions use the same restricted JSONata subset as source.where and are normalized identically (trimmed string coercion, the same coercion the parsers apply to scalar cells). A composite key is written with &, e.g. `source ID` & '|' & `mapping type`. A key expression that yields nothing, or an empty string, or a non-scalar, is an error naming the row: absence of a RELATION is data, absence of the KEY is a defect.

primary.description: Key expression over the primary row, evaluated at lookup time.

secondary.description: Key expression over a secondary row, evaluated once per secondary row at index-build time.

cardinality.title: Match cardinality
cardinality.description: Required, with no default, because cardinality is an assertion about the data rather than a preference: a default would make a wrong assumption invisible. There is no 'first': silently picking one of several matches would make output depend on source row order. 'one' binds the matched row as an object and is an error if two or more rows match. 'many' binds a LIST OF SCALARS, one per match, in secondary-collection order, and stays a list even when exactly one row matches. In BOTH modes, zero matches leaves the alias absent from the row rather than empty, so {alias.field|optional} handles a miss identically either way.

select.title: Selected secondary fields
select.description: With cardinality 'one', optional: narrows the bound object to these fields; omitted binds the whole matched row. With cardinality 'many', REQUIRED and must name exactly one field: the list binds that field's value from each match. A list of objects is deliberately not offered because template path traversal does not lift over arrays, and the template grammar is frozen. Every named field must exist somewhere in the secondary collection.

OntologyRef.description: Either an ontology id (e.g. 'nist_csf_2_0') or a CURIE prefix (e.g. 'csf:'). Per Ch 31a query-block schema.

ConceptRef.description: A CURIE for a concept node (e.g. 'csf:GV.OC-01') OR a wildcard '*'.

EdgePredicate.description: Edge type from the Crosswalker ontology: equivalent_to, broader_than, narrower_than, related_to, supports, etc. Extensible via plugins.

FieldSelector.description: Dotted property path against the in-memory model (e.g. 'concept.label', 'edge.weight', 'note.frontmatter.status').

AggregationOp.description: Built-in aggregation operators. Custom ops registered by Tier 2 helpers MUST start with 'x_'.

QueryFilter.description: A filter predicate — JSONata expression string OR a structured AND/OR/NOT tree. Per Ch 31a + Ch 36: JSONata is the only allowed string-expression slot in the schema.

Traversal.description: A graph traversal step. Subsumes single-hop and transitive walks via depth + transitive params (per Ch 29: closure folded into traverse).

on.description: Join predicate, typically an edge type or shared field.

kind.description: Join semantics. 'inner' (default): only rows where both sides match. 'left'/'right': preserve all rows from one side; null-pad the other on no match. 'outer': preserve all rows from both sides (full-outer). 'anti': Layer A primitive #5 — LEFT rows with NO match in 'with' ('X without Y' / gap analysis). See join-primitives.ts runtime.

QueryOutput.description: Where the query result lands. 'bases' compiles to a Bases view; 'codeblock' renders via crosswalker-pivot processor (deferred per D2); 'note' writes a generated note; 'inline' embeds in a host note as a ````base` block. 'tier2' means the query is answered by the SQL index and has no Bases form, which is required for anti-joins and aggregates: a Bases filter selects among notes that exist and therefore cannot report a relationship that is absent.

embed_in.description: If target=codeblock or inline, the host note path.

QueryViewOptions.description: Presentation hints. Kept narrow on purpose — query block does NOT specify column widths, colors, etc. (those belong in the .base file's view declaration).

PivotPrimitives.description: Pivot shape: rows × cols × cell. The launch-market 'Coverage Matrix' recipe instance composes filter+traverse+anti-join+pivot.

GraphPrimitives.description: Graph shape. Schema declared in v0.1.6; renderer (crosswalkerGraph custom view) ships v0.2 per Ch 30.

HierarchyPrimitives.description: Hierarchy shape. Schema declared in v0.1.6; renderer (crosswalkerHierarchy custom view) graduates v0.1.7-v0.1.8 per Ch 30.

TimelinePrimitives.description: Timeline shape. Schema declared in v0.1.6; renderer deferred to v0.2+ per Ch 30 (let Bases ship native timeline first).

ShapeDispatchA.description: Shape discriminator (style A): oneOf+const dispatch per Ch 31a. Each branch matches one shape and references its primitives sub-schema. Settings.recipeSchemaStyle='A' (default). Validation errors say 'must match exactly one schema' when shape doesn't match any branch.

ShapeDispatchB.description: Shape discriminator (style B): if/then/else dispatch per Ch 31b. Cascading conditional schemas; one allOf entry per shape. Settings.recipeSchemaStyle='B' (advanced). Validation errors are more focused on the specific failing shape branch instead of 'must match exactly one' (style A's failure mode). Semantically equivalent to style A; differs only in error messages and IDE autocomplete behavior.

query_block.description: Optional declarative query block (additive in SchemaVer 1.1.0; per Ch 31 + Ch 36). Recipes WITH `query:` declare what to query (axes, edges, aggregation) without writing SQL. Recipes WITHOUT `query:` continue to validate (additive). Engine compiles query + primitives to SQL recursive CTEs against the Tier 2 sqlite-wasm cache (per Ch 36 compositional language stack). The runtime is engine-neutral: a future Cozo/Oxigraph implementation could satisfy the same contract. JSONata is the only allowed string-expression language inside this block.

version.description: SchemaVer of the query block: MODEL.REVISION.ADDITION (Snowplow style). Increment ADDITION for new optional fields; REVISION for backward-compat semantic refinements; MODEL for breaking changes.

id.description: Stable identifier used by the Bases view, codeblock processor, and merge engine.

shape.description: View shape per Ch 30 v0.1 catalog. v0.1.6 ships pivot custom view + table/list (Bases-native). hierarchy graduates to custom view in v0.1.7-v0.1.8. graph + timeline are schema-declared but renderer ships v0.2+.

primitives.description: Shape-discriminated primitives sub-block. The `shape` field selects which primitives schema applies (see ShapeDispatchA / ShapeDispatchB).

params.description: Named parameters injectable at render time. Mirrors Datasette canned-query :name params.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema URI hint for editor autocomplete. Recipes typically set this to 'https://crosswalker.dev/spec/recipe.schema.json' so VS Code / IntelliJ resolve the schema for validation + autocomplete. Not load-bearing for plugin runtime — Crosswalker validates against the bundled schema regardless of what value is here.

$comment.description: Optional free-text comment for recipe authors. Ignored by the validator and runtime. Useful for explaining why a recipe was authored, what it depends on, what it's for.

recipe.description: Recipe identifier. Stable across re-runs. Used in _crosswalker.recipe.id provenance. Examples: 'nist-80053r5-allfolders', 'iso27001-mostly-headings', 'mitre-attack-tag-driven'.

spec_version.description: URI of the recipe spec this recipe conforms to. Optional in the recipe file (defaults to current spec); required when serializing a recipe for portability across producer ecosystems.

source.title: Source declaration
source.description: What ontology this recipe imports. Out-of-scope: where the source bytes come from (file path, URL) — that's the producer's input, not the recipe's concern.

ontology.description: Source ontology identifier. Convention: lowercase ASCII slug. Examples: 'nist-800-53-r5', 'iso27001', 'mitre-attack', 'cri-profile-2.0'.

version.description: Compatibility declaration for the source ontology version. This is not proof of the selected source bytes. Verified run metadata remains authoritative; this declaration may be used only as an explicit fallback when no verified version is known. Excluded from the effective target hash.

levels.description: Ordered sequence of source-level identifiers, outer to inner. The recipe.target.layout array must declare a layout_entry for each level (or fewer, if some levels are flattened by the layout). Examples for NIST 800-53 r5: ['catalog', 'family', 'control', 'enhancement']. For a biology taxonomy: ['domain', 'kingdom', 'phylum', 'class', 'order', 'family', 'genus', 'species'].

detect.title: Source recognition hints
detect.description: Optional hints that let a wizard recognize a raw source file and SUGGEST how to read it. Hints never select anything on their own; the wizard offers, the user confirms. Column-signature matching (derived from target.layout) remains the identity test. Excluded from the effective target hash; included in the recipe document digest like the rest of source.

sheet.description: Preferred worksheet name when the source is a workbook. Exact match, case-sensitive, after trimming.

sheet_aliases.description: Alternative worksheet names seen in other releases of the same source. Matched the same way as sheet.

header_row.description: 0-based index of the header row on the preferred sheet, skipping banner rows above it. Same convention as source.joins.from.header_row.

filename.description: Case-insensitive substrings expected in the source filename (for example "CRI", "Profile"). A hint only: raises rank among candidates that already match by columns; never admits a candidate by itself.

notes.description: One or two sentences shown to the user beside the suggestion: where the file comes from, which download to pick.

nest.description: Declares that the primary collection's records own sub-record lists, and that each level should become its own rows. Level 0 is the primary iterator's records. CONTRACT (any producer that follows it hash-matches the plugin): (1) emission is depth-first in document order, parent row before its children, then the next parent; a `leaf: none` row is not emitted; its children still carry `_cw.parent`; (2) every emitted row carries one reserved key `_cw`, an object with `level` (this level's name), `path` (array of ancestor ids root first, including self), `parent` (the immediate parent's id, or '' at level 0), and `ancestors.<level>.<field>` (the carried fields of each ancestor AND of this row's own level); (3) identity 'path' joins escaped pieces with '/'; (4) leaf 'folder-note' lands at <folder>/<folder>.md; (5) source.where is evaluated per emitted row after `_cw` is attached and does not cascade from parent to child; (5b) when source.where excludes a parent, every carried field of that excluded ancestor is blanked to '' on admitted descendants so its folder level renders empty and records folder-level-skipped; (6) a record at a level whose leaf is 'section' is not emitted as a row; it is attached to its nearest emitted ancestor under _cw.sections in document order, and rendered inside that ancestor's managed body region, after the ancestor's own body projections, as one heading region per record (heading text from that level's layout heading entry, depth from its level_depth, content from body projections declared with that level), with section levels below a section level rendered depth-first as deeper headings. The last entry has no children. Participates in the recipe hash because it changes which notes exist.

where.title: Row predicate
where.description: Optional JSONata predicate over one source row. A row for which it is false never becomes a note. MUST evaluate to a boolean; anything else is an error naming the row and the expression, never a silent skip. Every field name it references must exist in the source collection, and a predicate that admits zero rows from a non-empty source is an error. Restricted subset: field references, string/number/true/false/null literals, array literals, the operators = != < <= > >= in and or &, and the functions $not $exists $trim $lowercase $uppercase $string $number $contains(value, 'literal'). The second $contains argument must be a string literal; a missing or non-string first argument evaluates to false, and regex and dynamic patterns are forbidden. Regular expressions, lambdas and dynamic field access are rejected, so an external producer in another language can reimplement the same predicate exactly. Values are compared as the parser produced them (spreadsheet cells are strings), so numeric intent must be explicit: $number(count) > 5. Runs BEFORE identity, CURIE minting, concept_cid and render(). Participates in the recipe hash because it changes which notes exist. Absent means every row becomes a note (behaviour before SchemaVer 1.9.0).

joins.title: Keyed lookup enrichment
joins.description: Optional named secondary collections, each indexed by a key expression, whose matched rows become addressable on the primary row under the alias. The object key IS the alias. An alias never merges into the row's own namespace and never shadows a source column: the row gains exactly one new key, so a joined field is reached by the dotted traversal and ['literal key'] quoting that already exist and the template grammar needs no change. Runs AFTER source.where and BEFORE identity, CURIE minting, concept_cid and render(). Participates in the recipe hash because it changes what a row is and therefore what the notes assert. The primary collection is still consumed row by row; only the secondary collection is held in memory. Absent means no secondary collections (behaviour before SchemaVer 1.9.0).

propertyNames.description: Alias. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, so it is addressable as a bare template segment with no quoting.

target.title: Target structure
target.description: How the recipe projects source data into Tier 1 vault structure. The render() function consumes this object plus a concept-identity record and produces an Address (path + wikilink target + tags + aliases + frontmatter). Pass 1 is vault-independent (deterministic, hashable); Pass 2 (link minimizer) is opt-in via linkStyle: shortest.

layout.description: Ordered list, one entry per source level (outer-to-inner). The recipe author chooses each level's mechanism: which Obsidian primitive carries that level's hierarchy. Five mechanisms admitted by v0.1; folder/file/heading wired; tag/wikilink reserved for v0.2.

also_emit.title: Cross-cutting emissions (parallel to layout)
also_emit.description: Repeated for every output note: tags, aliases, frontmatter the recipe writes alongside the layout. Default behavior: dual-emit (folder layout + parallel tags) per the SEACOW pattern + Ranganathan faceted-classification rationale (Ch 22 §4 + §9).

tags.description: Tag-path templates emitted into every note's tags array. Example: ['framework/nist/{family.id|lower}/{control.id|tagsafe}', 'cross-cutting/access-control'].

aliases.description: Alias templates emitted into every note's aliases array. Used by Obsidian alias resolution; helps wikilinks like [[AC-2]] resolve to the correct file even if the file is named differently. Example: ['{control.id}', '{control.title}'].

body.description: Ordered recipe-managed body projections. Entries are evaluated by pure render() against row scope. Only append and section positions are portable in this schema version; workbench table-row output and legacy transforms are rejected rather than silently coerced or dropped.

graph_edges.description: Frontmatter-encoded named relationships. Schema-reserved in v0.1 (validators warn 'graph_edges deferred to v0.2; ignored'); wired in v0.2.

crosswalks.description: Cross-ontology references packed into a column of a concept source. Each entry produces crosswalk-edge notes (Tier 1 crosswalk_edge_frontmatter) in their own import set under the sssom identity prefix; nothing is written into the concept note. Distinct from graph_edges, which encode intra-ontology relations as frontmatter properties on the concept note.

auto_heading.title: Automatic H1 heading control
auto_heading.description: Controls the automatic H1 the generation engine prepends to a note body. A template string sets the heading text (rendered against the row scope, same grammar as any other template). `false` suppresses the heading entirely. Omitted preserves existing behaviour exactly: an H1 derived from the note title/identifier, emitted on the recipe path always and on the wizard path only when body content exists. Placed on `target` rather than inside `also_emit` so a workbench round trip preserves it for free, because patchOwnedRegions replaces `also_emit` wholesale. Additive, SchemaVer 1.8.0; recipes without this key are unaffected and hash byte-identically.

linkStyle.description: Wikilink rendering style. 'absolute': always emit full-path form 'Folder/Sub/AC-2'; deterministic; hashable; what the canonical-state hash is computed against. 'shortest': downgrade to bare basename when unambiguous in the target vault; requires Pass 2 of render() with a VaultIndex; non-deterministic across users; deferred to v0.3.

query.description: Optional declarative query block (additive in SchemaVer 1.1.0; per Ch 31 + Ch 36). Recipes WITHOUT `query:` continue to validate; recipes WITH `query:` declare what to query (axes, edges, aggregation) using the 8-verb Layer A primitive vocabulary (per Ch 29). The engine compiles the query+primitives to SQL recursive CTEs against the Tier 2 sqlite-wasm cache. Engine-neutral schema; runtime-portable to Cozo/Oxigraph/etc. JSONata is the only allowed string-expression language inside this block. See `$defs.query_block` for the full schema.

examples.$comment: Recipe (a) from Ch 22 §2.2: All-folders (the v0.1 default).
Recipe (b) from Ch 22 §2.2: Mostly-headings (single-document feel). Catalog becomes a single .md file; family/control/enhancement are nested headings inside it.
Recipe (e) from Ch 22 §2.2: Hybrid (the realistic case). Folder for catalog/family, file for control, heading for enhancement.
